topics.topic: How an OwnerFormField row identifies a closed list and maps submitted text to a member value
questions: Where does a row identify the particular closed list and the member-value mapping used to parse its text?
Where does a row identify the particular closed list and the mapping from submitted text to its member value?
What identifies the particular closed list and maps submitted text to one of its members?

quotes:
A row's `name` is
  the field's name: its path in the `OwnerRequest` or `OwnerValues` it fills
  (`carrier`), parts joined by a full stop, with a tuple's position written
  where the row holds `OWNER_FORM_POSITION_MARK` (`#`), as decimal digits
  from 0. A row's `reads_as` says how the field's text is read: as the text
  itself, an integer's decimal digits, `true` or `false`, or an enumeration
  member's value.
judgement.why: State 6 makes the row name identify the destination model field, whose enumeration supplies the particular closed list, and maps submitted text to that enumeration member's value.

quotes:
A row's `name` is
  the field's name: its path in the `OwnerRequest` or `OwnerValues` it fills
  (`carrier`), parts joined by a full stop, with a tuple's position written
  where the row holds `OWNER_FORM_POSITION_MARK` (`#`), as decimal digits
  from 0.

A union's fields are the rows of all its variants, and its
  discriminator chooses the variant.

The table holds the names the generator would
  otherwise derive from the models, and pages write the same names (Route
  B runs of 2026-11-25: six samples each derived them differently; owner,
  2026-11-25).
judgement.why: State 6 selects a row by its carrier-qualified complete model path, uses the union discriminator where variants share a carrier, and requires pages to emit those table names rather than introducing a separate page or action scope.

topics.topic: Which owner inputs OWNER_FORM_FIELDS covers, including query, hidden, repeated, and other non-visible fields
questions: Does OWNER_FORM_FIELDS still describe owner query fields, or are query parameters excluded and specified elsewhere?
Does OWNER_FORM_FIELDS also describe owner inputs carried in query parameters, or only submitted form controls?
Does OWNER_FORM_FIELDS cover only visible user-entered controls, or also hidden form fields, CSRF fields, target parameters, query parameters, and repeated controls that the interface reads?

quotes:
The target is the query parameter
  `OWNER_TARGET_PARAMETER` (`target`) names, an identity and never a
  personal value (R0-29). A `GET` request's other fields are its query's, a
  `POST` request's the fields of its `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
  body, or of the upload's multipart head. Every other field is a row of the
  data provider's `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` (`OwnerFormField`).

The CSRF value is the field
  `OWNER_CSRF_FIELD` (`csrf`) names, the upload's first part included, and
  `OwnerRequest.csrf_value` carries it from the form's reading to the
  request's admission, since a body is read once.

A form that repeats a name,
  gives a text the row's `reads_as` cannot read or leaves a gap in a tuple's
  positions cannot be read.
judgement.why: State 6 separately names the target and CSRF fields, places other GET query and POST body or multipart-head fields in OWNER_FORM_FIELDS, and declares repeated names unreadable.

questions: What exact lexical forms, normalization, and failure rules define whole-number, yes-or-no, and closed-list parsing?
What exact input grammar and failure behavior apply to whole numbers and yes/no values?

quotes:
A row's `reads_as` says how the field's text is read: as the text
  itself, an integer's decimal digits, `true` or `false`, or an enumeration
  member's value.

A field the form leaves out is none,
  and a tuple none of whose positions are given is empty. A field whose name
  no row names is not read and changes nothing. A form that repeats a name,
  gives a text the row's `reads_as` cannot read or leaves a gap in a tuple's
  positions cannot be read.

A
  request whose body, upload head or form cannot be read is handed on with
  no values, no CSRF value and no credential (option (a) of the question
  State 4 carried to State 7, round-51 and round-55 T3).
judgement.why: State 6 fixes the accepted scalar and member spellings, defines absence, repetition and parse failure, and states how an unreadable form is handed onward.

topics.topic: Whether every submitted field must have exactly one row and how unlisted fields are handled
questions: Must the release prove that every page field has exactly one row, and what must the reader do with a submitted field that has no row?

quotes:
A field whose name
  no row names is not read and changes nothing. A form that repeats a name,
  gives a text the row's `reads_as` cannot read or leaves a gap in a tuple's
  positions cannot be read. The table holds the names the generator would
  otherwise derive from the models, and pages write the same names (Route
  B runs of 2026-11-25: six samples each derived them differently; owner,
  2026-11-25).
judgement.why: State 6 requires pages to use the table's names, makes an unlisted submitted field inert, and makes a repeated listed name unreadable.
